newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-ST ANDREWS WITNESSES WAR OF WORDS BETWEEN PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ST ANDREWS WITNESSES WAR OF WORDS BETWEEN PLAYERS.

text.p: The sacred turf of St Andrews' Old Course became the unlikely scene of a golfing rarity -- a bitter exchange between two players -- when U.S. money leader Phil Mickelson and Swede Jarmo Sandelin clashed at the Dunhill Cup on Sunday.
World number nine Mickelson accused his semifinal opponent of a lack of sportsmanship and said he was upset by Sandelin's celebrations every time he made a putt.
The American felt Sandelin was being disrespectful -- and told him so.
"On the 12th tee Mickelson came to me and said 'You should show me some respect and don't behave like that'," Sandelin, who has played on the U.S. Tour this year, said.
"He said this is a friendly game. I said I know it is but I want to win my game.

"Then he criticised my play in the U.S. Tour this year," Sandelin said. "I know I have been playing badly there and that's true. But just because he's in the top 10 in the world rankings doesn't mean he can say things like that."
Sandelin, five under par through 12 holes, said he was happy to make his putts "and I probably showed it. But I did nothing really. I just showed I was pleased when I holed the putts.
"He was four behind and maybe it made him upset. We shook hands at the end. I think he was over-reacting."
Sandelin won the match 68-71 but the U.S. won the semifinal tie on victories by Mark O'Meara and Steve Stricker over Peter Hedblom and Patrick Sjoland respectively.
Mickelson said his remarks were sparked by Sandelin's reaction to the Swede's extra hole defeat of Zimbabwe's Nick Price on Friday.

The 26-year-old American refused to discuss the events at the 12th directly but said: "I feel the Dunhill Cup, Ryder Cup and President's Cup are wonderful events that promote sportsmanship and camaraderie internationally.
"I think it's important to keep those events in high esteem and to promote good sportsmanship."
Mickelson said that when Sandelin beat Price "it could have been handled better than it was by the Swede.
"I think Nick Price is a wonderful diplomat to the game of golf and I think he has been nothing but nice to me and to everybody else.
"I feel that our match could have been conducted with a little more sportsmanship and I was disappointed," he added.

But the two players patched up their differences afterwards. "Everything is fine now," Mickelson said. "He's a wonderful player. It is too bad he won't be able to keep playing on the U.S. Tour because he wasn't able to keep his card.
"I'm sure he'll have a wonderful year next year on the European Tour."
